name: Clyde Schmidt
life: “I still remember walking into a port office under somebody else's lucky number.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Clyde by a small Wednesday habit. Clyde starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I am the younger hand who gets the vacancy. I am proud of it and have promised them their old table whenever they visit.
appearance: Clyde has auburn hair cut square at the nape, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a comb in a sleeve sewn into the lining. When somebody else has the floor, Clyde gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Clyde has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To keep visiting rights at the old table.
family: Jasmine Miranda is Clyde’s second cousin. Clyde is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Jasmine calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *An address in pencil*, Jasmine says, “I wanted the house number on a necklace so my mother can tell a driver where she lives.”
connections: Stanley Hull. The foreman's hour gives the younger hand a real chance to work beside the departing crew.

reactions.situation: The two old workers are offered separate farewell days
reactions.response: Clyde asks each worker separately what kind of last day they want.

reactions.situation: An envelope of wages is found under a café chair
reactions.response: Clyde finds a second person to witness its return so an honest mistake won't cost a worker their pay.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Clyde says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
